entry.title: UC Davis Water Polo Athlete: Saving Lives and Academic Success | Face to Face with Chancellor May

media:group.media:title: UC Davis Water Polo Athlete: Saving Lives and Academic Success | Face to Face with Chancellor May
media:group.media:description:
In this episode of Face to Face, Chancellor May talks with UC Davis mechanical and aerospace engineering student and water polo athlete Lillie Vehling about rescuing three girls from drowning, co-founding Swim Ags to provide free adult swim and water safety lessons, and her future work in the Navy’s nuclear propulsion program. Lillie also shares how she balances academics and athletics, her water polo team’s goals for the upcoming season and a few personal favorites with Chancellor May.
*Timestamps* 1:04 Lillie’s heroic effort saving three young girls from drowning in Seattle 2:18 Teaching swim and water safety to adults of all ages and levels within UC Davis 3:29 Post-graduation pursuit in the Naval Propulsion Officer candidate program 4:34 Key advice for balancing goals as a D1 athlete and STEM student 5:19 Academic support as a D1 athlete at UC Davis 5:40 Predictions for the UC Davis Women’s Water Polo team in its first year in the Golden Coast Conference 7:38 How Chancellor May uses engineering in his everyday life 8:04 Does Chancellor May swim?
*About UC Davis Chancellor Gary S. May* Gary S. May became UC Davis’ seventh chancellor on Aug. 1, 2017. An accomplished scholar and engineer, May came to UC Davis from the Georgia Institute of Technology. More at: https://leadership.ucdavis.edu/chancellor/gary-s-may?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=chancellor_fltl
*Follow Chancellor May* Bluesky: https://bsky.app/profile/chancellormay.bsky.social Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/ChancellorMay/ Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/chancellor.may/ Twitter/X: https://x.com/chancellor_may
*All UC Davis Podcasts and Shows* https://www.ucdavis.edu/news/podcasts-and-shows?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=chancellor_fltl
*Check Out UC Davis* Website: https://www.ucdavis.edu/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=chancellor_fltl Virtual campus tour: https://www.ucdavis.edu/about/visit/campus-virtual-tour/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=chancellor_fltl
*About UC Davis* Since the beginning, we’ve outgrown expectations. Established in 1908 as a university farm, UC Davis has continually branched out, challenged the way things are done, and gained recognition for solving complex problems related to health, environment, culture and society. Our 5,300-acre campus borders the city of Davis, a vibrant college town of about 68,000 people in Yolo County.
UC Davis is among the most comprehensive campuses in the University of California system, with four colleges and six professional schools that offer over 100 undergraduate majors and more than 100 graduate and professional degrees. UC Davis enrolls about 40,000 students from over 110 countries and contributes at least $13 billion to the California economy each year. In the 2024-25 fiscal year, the university exceeded $1 billion in research funding for the third consecutive year, cementing its reputation as a tier one research university.

entry.title: Setting Olive Oil Standards with UC Davis Research

media:group.media:title: Setting Olive Oil Standards with UC Davis Research
media:group.media:description:
What makes California olive oil worth a closer look? Mary Mori of California Olive Ranch explains how UC Davis Olive Center research helped California producers gain global attention and challenged the quality of imported olive oils.
A major 2010 study raised questions about whether the olive oil on store shelves lived up to its label. Mori shares what that research meant for California’s olive oil industry. She also explains how federally funded research helps reveal the chemistry of California olive oils and demonstrate their quality.
This video is part of From Labs to Lives, a UC Davis series showing how research shapes everyday life.
Learn more at https://ucdav.is/UCDOilResearch
Video description: Mary Mori, Vice President of Quality and Product at California Olive Ranch, speaks to the camera with a mix of b-roll of olive trees, olives and olive oil shown throughout the video.

*THE VALUE OF RESEARCH* This video is part of From Labs to Lives, a UC Davis series showing how research shapes everyday life: https://www.ucdavis.edu/research/labs-to-lives?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=labs-to-lives
*VISUAL DESCRIPTION* Green olives hang from a sunlit branch. Harvested olives tumble onto metal rollers. Golden olive oil pours from a green glass bottle into a red-and-white patterned bowl. An aerial view shows long rows of olive trees across gently rolling land. A closer overhead shot shows a harvesting machine transferring olives into a trailer pulled by a tractor. In the orchard, a woman wearing a white California Olive Ranch shirt examines an olive between her fingers. Inside a bottling facility, green glass bottles travel along a conveyor beneath mechanical arms. More bottles pass through enclosed equipment. A shelf displays California Olive Ranch extra virgin olive oils with different colored labels. The woman appears on camera in front of large metal tanks. Yellow text identifies her as “Mary Mori, Vice President of Quality and Product, California Olive Ranch.” The view shifts to strips of green-and-white labels running through a labeling machine, then to finished bottles moving along a curved conveyor. An aerial shot returns to the orchard, where harvesting equipment works between the rows. Mori looks down at olives in her hands. In another close-up, a hand lets green and purple olives fall onto processing equipment. A cluster of green olives hangs among narrow leaves. A wide aerial view shows straight orchard rows stretching toward the horizon, with power lines in the distance. The final shots show bottles labeled “California Olive Ranch Extra Virgin Olive Oil — Global Blend” on a shelf, followed by capped bottles passing beneath machinery on the production line.
